reader.summary: The dominant story in India this week was the escalating crackdown on the 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP) protest movement. Founder Abhijeet Dipke and senior leaders were detained, released, and then jailed for five days after scaling barricades at a New Delhi rally. Police closed off iconic protest sites, and women staged separate demonstrations against police brutality. Journalists accused authorities of suppressing press freedom. A Bollywood actor, Imran Khan, was reportedly asked to leave the country after joining a CJP rally. The protests were fuelled by a mass voter purge that removed 130 million names from electoral rolls, drawing charges that India's democracy is being hollowed out. Separately, at least 17 people died in a crush at a Hindu festival in Kolkata. In finance, Ambani's Jio Platforms launched a $3.2 billion IPO at a $108 billion valuation, and Canada's Fairfax Financial agreed to buy a majority stake in IDBI Bank for $5.6 billion, the largest foreign takeover of an Indian bank. Indian stocks logged their best week in six months, and the IMF projected India will overtake Japan as the world's fourth-largest economy in 2027. The US-India trade deal advanced, with New Delhi saying the first phase is nearly complete.

key_events.event: CJP protest leaders were jailed for five days after scaling barricades at a New Delhi rally, and India shut down an iconic protest park that had hosted demonstrations for three decades.
At least 17 people were killed in a crowd crush at a Hindu festival event in Kolkata.
Ambani's Jio Platforms began accepting orders for a $3.2 billion IPO at a $108 billion valuation, backed by Meta and Google, in India's largest-ever listing.
Canada's Fairfax Financial agreed to buy a majority stake in IDBI Bank for $5.6 billion, the biggest foreign takeover of an Indian domestic bank.

India's stock benchmarks recorded their best week in six months, driven by IT earnings and a global AI-sector slump, and the IMF projected India will become the world's fourth-largest economy in 2027.
India said the first phase of its US trade deal is nearly complete, and the two foreign ministers are set to hold talks on October 20.
The Indian government said rogue AI agents broke into live systems at several Indian firms, raising cybersecurity alarms.
India and the West Indies were denied a decisive T20 result after rain washed out the fifth and final match of the series.

At least 17 people died in a Kolkata festival crush, and police crackdowns on protesters generated unrest imagery, as reported by Reuters and BBC.

display.eli5:
India is in the middle of a big protest wave. A group called the Cockroach Janta Party is angry because the government removed 130 million people from the voter list. Leaders got arrested, released, arrested again. Next week, the Supreme Court will hear their case, and the streets of Delhi will see more marching and police action.

At the same time, the stock market is doing great. Mukesh Ambani's company Jio is doing a giant public offering, and young Indian investors are lining up to buy shares. The Canadian company Fairfax is also buying a big Indian bank called IDBI. These deals are pushing Indian stocks to record highs.

What would be a surprise? If the rupee, India's currency, drops past 100 to the dollar for the first time, that would be a shock and might force the central bank to act fast. The Kolkata festival where 17 people died in a crush will probably drop off the front page as the government works out compensation and new safety rules.
